name: Dick Moore
role: De Morès associate indicted in the Luffsey killing
bio: Dick Moore was named in September 1885 with Frank Miller in the indictment for the killing of Luffsey, though his whereabouts were then unknown, and the paper predicted acquittal if he were tried. In 1886 he brought two Siberian bloodhounds from New York for the Marquis de Morès's bear hunts, went with the Marquis to Powder river, and in July married Lizzie Hannon in St. Paul.

mentions: …en persons were subpœnaed as witnesses in the case of the Territory vs. Marquis de Mores, E. G. Paddock, Dick Moore and Frank Miller, and left for Bismarck from here last Monday morning.
Dick Moore and Frank Miller have been included in the indictment for the killing of Luffsey. Their whereabouts is at present unknown, and it is doubtful if they will be present at…
…on the same evidence that acquitted the Marquis. This will probably set the whole matter at rest, as, even if Moore and Miller are tried they must be acquitted.
Dick Moore, well-known to old-timers, arrived Sunday from New York, having in charge two pure-bred Siberian blood-hounds. They will be used by the Marquis in hunting bear.
…quis de Mores has gone to Powder river to look up some of the cross Y steers and other business matters. Dick Moore accompanied him.
Dick Moore left for the east Saturday morning. His last stop here is the longest he has ever made in one place since he was a boy.
Dick Moore and Lizzie Hannon who left for the east ten days ago, were marmaried in St. Paul last week.
